findings.title: Data races on shared err and totalBatchesIndexed inside errgroup goroutines
findings.body: In searchSupport.init, each goroutine spawned by group.Go writes to the outer shared variables: `totalBatchesIndexed++` (line 189) and `_, _, err = s.build(...)` (line 190). These run concurrently with up to initWorkers goroutines and with the main goroutine which reads/overwrites `err` at `err = group.Wait()`. This is an unsynchronized read/write race (flagged by -race) on both `err` and `totalBatchesIndexed`, and the span attribute count can be undercounted. Use an atomic counter (or collect per-goroutine) and return the build error only via the goroutine's return value instead of assigning to the shared err.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the cache map without holding cacheMu
findings.body: TotalDocs ranges over b.cache with no lock, while BuildIndex now writes b.cache[key] under cacheMu at line 138 and GetIndex reads under RLock. Previously BuildIndex held cacheMu for its whole duration, so writes only happened while no other BuildIndex was running, but TotalDocs was still unsafe — and this PR makes it worse by calling TotalDocs from searchSupport.init's new log line and by allowing concurrent builds. A concurrent map read and write panics at runtime. TotalDocs should take b.cacheMu.RLock() while iterating.

findings.title: Removing the BuildIndex lock allows duplicate concurrent builds of the same key
findings.body: BuildIndex previously held cacheMu for the entire function, which serialized builds. Now the lock is only taken when inserting into the cache, and getOrCreateIndex in search.go has no per-key locking (its own TODO acknowledges this). Two concurrent requests (or a request plus a watch event) for the same NamespacedResource can both see GetIndex return nil, both run a full bleve build, and both assign b.cache[key] — the loser's index is never closed (file handles/disk for file-backed indexes leak) and duplicate work is done. A per-key build mutex or singleflight is needed to keep the finer-grained locking safe.

findings.title: Init failure in NewResourceServer leaks the cancelable context
findings.body: NewResourceServer creates ctx/cancel, then calls s.Init(ctx) and returns nil, err on failure without calling cancel(). The background context and its goroutine resources are never released on the error path. Call cancel() before returning the error.
